title: Olivia and the Hidden Jump
subtitle: Energy can hide, then run
author: Olivia's Shelf
blurb: Olivia winds a little toy that sits still — then hops — and learns that energy can hide in a spring, a high-up ball, or a bite of lunch.

magic.launch: The little rocket pushed the air, and the air pushed back.
magic.drop: Everything falls. That pull has a name: gravity.

openai.instructions: Warm, clear storyteller reading a science picture book to a child. Curious, never lecturing. Pause at full stops.

pages.heading: A still toy
pages.text: {Olivia} wound a little toy. It sat still. Then it {hopped}. "{Elon:elon/look}," she said. "Where was the jump hiding?"

pages.heading: Energy can hide
pages.text: "{Energy} can hide," said {Elon:elon/teach}. "In a wound spring. In a ball held high. In a tight rubber band."

pages.heading: Then it runs
pages.text: Olivia let the ball drop. Hidden energy became a {fall}. "Let go, and hidden energy {runs}," said Elon.

pages.heading: Lunch is a store
pages.text: "{Food} hides energy for your body," said {Elon:elon/teach}. "The Sun hides energy in {light}."

pages.heading: Energy changes clothes
pages.text: "Energy does not vanish," said Elon. "It changes {clothes}. A hop. A glow. A little heat."

pages.heading: Keep asking why
pages.text: "Why does a bounced ball get lower each time?" asked {Olivia:olivia/ask}. "Some energy becomes {heat} in the floor," said {Elon:elon/teach}.

end.heading: The End
end.text: Energy can hide, then run. It does not vanish. It changes clothes.
end.prompt: What would you wind, lift, or bounce tomorrow?

credits: Painted for Olivia's Shelf. Elon is a picture-book inventor who teaches physics; this is not a biography.

questions.right: Yes! Energy can store, then move.
questions.wrong: Elon said energy can hide, then run.

options.label: in a wound spring or a high ball

questions.right: That's right. Springs and high-up things store energy.
questions.wrong: A wound spring and a ball held high both hide energy.

questions.q: Why does a bounced ball get lower?
questions.right: Yes. Some of the jump becomes heat in the floor.
questions.wrong: Some energy becomes heat, so the next bounce is smaller.
